identificationModule.officialTitle: Safety and Efficacy of CD19/CD22 Dual Targeted CAR-T Cell Therapy in Patients With R/R B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

descriptionModule.detailedDescription: CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. CD19 and CD22 are proteins usually expressed on the surface of the B leukemia cells. The dual-CARs enables the T-cells to recognize and kill the tumor cell through recognition of CD19 and CD22.

primaryOutcomes.description: To evaluate the possible adverse events that could occurred within the first month post SL19+22 infusion, including symptoms such as cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity.
Remission Rate includes complete remission(CR)、CR with incomplete blood count recovery(CRi)、No remission(NR)

secondaryOutcomes.description: the copy number of CD19 and CD22 CAR- T cells in the genomes of peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) by quantitative Real-time PCR (qPCR).
Cytokine( IL-6,IL-10,IFN-γ,TNF-α ) concentration (pg/mL) by flow cytometry
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: First month post CAR-T cells infusion
